subject.title: fix(hooks): wire message:sending internal hook to user-defined hooks

question: Should OpenClaw add an internal pre-send observer event, and if so must it observe pre-policy intent or the final post-policy content that will actually be delivered?
rationale: Current documentation reserves blocking and modification for typed plugin hooks, while this PR creates a new trusted-code observation boundary whose timing determines whether canceled or rewritten content is exposed and what audit records mean.

options.title: Post-Policy Observer
options.body: Add a canonical `message:sending` observer after typed policy resolves, emitting final deliverable content exactly once and doing nothing for canceled messages.

options.title: Explicit Intent Event
options.body: Expose pre-policy content under a clearly named intent event with documentation that it may never be delivered and may contain unredacted data.

options.title: Keep Typed Hooks Only
options.body: Do not add an internal pre-send event and direct filtering, cancellation, and outbound policy use cases to typed plugin hooks.

recommendation.title: Post-Policy Observer
recommendation.body: Add a canonical `message:sending` observer after typed policy resolves, emitting final deliverable content exactly once and doing nothing for canceled messages.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history spans both the internal-hook contract and the outbound delivery boundary.
